items.text: Its first cover idea showed Marvin the Martian aiming a raygun at Earth, until legal trouble ruled it out.
items.why: Background and release: 'An early cover art proposal for the album included Marvin the Martian pointing a raygun at the Earth. This was eventually discarded due to legal problems.' The pack says 'an early' proposal, not the first one.

items.text: Homestead, Touch and Go
items.why: Infobox 'Labels: Homestead Touch and Go'.

items.text: Steve Albini (guitar, vocals, drum machine programming), Santiago Durango (guitar), Dave Riley (bass guitar)
items.why: Personnel: 'Steve Albini – guitar, vocals, drum machine programming; Santiago Durango – guitar; Dave Riley – bass guitar'.

items.text: Atomizer was Big Black's first full-length album.
items.why: Lead: 'the debut full-length album by American punk rock group Big Black'.

items.text: Before it came out, 'Big Money' was the B-side of the 'Il Duce' single.
items.why: Background and release: '"Big Money", was released as a B-side to the "Il Duce" single prior to the release of Atomizer'.

items.text: Homestead also put 'Big Money' and 'Il Duce' on a promo record with three live songs, under an agreement that it be used only for promotion.
items.why: Background and release: 'Homestead Records also issued "Big Money" and "Il Duce" the A-side of a 12" record with three live songs on the B-side ... with the agreement that the 12" be used for promotional purposes only.'

items.text: The label sent it to radio stations, then sold extra copies outside Chicago, and the band found out.
items.why: Background and release: 'The label sent the promo 12" to radio stations, then sold extra copies outside of Big Black's native Chicago, hoping the band would never find out. When they did'.

items.text: The band left Homestead and signed with Touch and Go.
items.why: Background and release: 'Big Black left Homestead and signed to Touch and Go Records.'

items.text: Dave Riley was new to the band for this album, and Andy Kellman called his bass lumberjack-like.
items.why: Music and lyrics, Kellman: 'new member Dave Riley's lumberjack bass'.

items.text: The credits list Roland alongside the band members, though Roland is a drum machine brand and not a person.
items.why: Personnel: 'Big Black always credited Roland along with the band's members, though Roland is a brand of drum machine and not an actual person.' (The pack also says, flagged citation needed, that Atomizer used an E-mu Drumulator rather than the TR-606.)

items.text: The following year the band recorded the four-song Headache EP, and its sticker warned buyers that it fell short of Atomizer.
items.why: Background and release: 'In the year after Atomizer's release, Big Black recorded their 4-song Headache EP and released it with a sticker that bore the words, "Warning! Not as good as Atomizer"'.

items.text: That same year, Atomizer was put on CD with the Headache EP and the 'Heartbeat' single, under the title The Rich Man's Eight Track Tape.
items.why: Background and release: 'That same year Atomizer was compiled onto compact disc along with the Headache EP and the band's "Heartbeat" single under the name, The Rich Man's Eight Track Tape.'

items.text: The CD left off 'Strange Things', which a later reissue restored, and had none of the original artwork or liner notes.
items.why: Background and release: 'The CD omitted track 9 "Strange Things" (although included in a subsequent reissue), as well as the artwork and liner notes from the original records.'

items.text: Steve Albini used the CD's liner notes to say he disliked the format, and told readers to scratch the discs and eat sandwiches off them.
items.why: Background and release: 'Steve Albini expressed his general dislike for the compact disc format in the CD's liner notes ... scratch them, fingerprint them, and eat egg and bacon sandwiches off them.'

items.text: In May 2011 St. Vincent played a live cover of 'Kerosene' at Bowery Ballroom in New York.
items.why: Notable covers: 'St. Vincent performed live at the Our Band Could Be Your Life 10th Anniversary Show at New York's Bowery Ballroom on May 22, 2011'.

items.text: Andy Kellman says its guitar intro cannot be accurately described by imitating it with your voice or with gestures.
items.why: Music and lyrics: 'Kellman described the guitar intro of the latter track as "completely incapable of being accurately described by vocal imitation or physical gesture."' Title matches the track list.

items.text: Its guitar work has been described as warped beyond recognition.
items.why: Music and lyrics: 'The guitar work on the tracks "Passing Complexion" and "Kerosene" have been described as "warped-beyond-recognition."' Title matches the track list.

items.text: Andy Kellman believes it may be a reply, perhaps unintended, to John Mellencamp's 'Pink Houses'.
items.why: Music and lyrics: 'Kellman also stated his belief that the track "Bad Houses" could be "a perhaps unintentional reply" to "Pink Houses" by John Mellencamp.' Title matches the track list.

missed: The overall sound: two guitars, bass and a drum machine, which Kellman calls 'assaultive Roland beats' with 'clanging and whirring guitars', and the lead calls a forerunner of industrial rock. Also that the opener 'Jordan, Minnesota' is controversial for lyrics told from the perpetrators' side of a child abuse case, which a listener may want warning of.
